audionova.name: AudioNova
audionova.summary: Local A.I voice generation and transformation, powered by Qualcomm Whisper optimized for Snapdragon X.

event.title: Devpost Software Showcase — Staff Picks & Rails

inspiration_intel.the_wedge: Their starting insight: Cloud TTS forces a trade between privacy, latency and cost, and nobody teaches the on-device path. They targeted people who already have a finished script and no interest in learning prompt engineering.
inspiration_intel.what_it_does: Windows app with two modes: generate speech from text with one of five built-in voices or a cloned voice, and re-voice any uploaded or recorded clip. Transcription and synthesis both run on the Snapdragon X device.
steal_this: Put the model on the device and make connectivity a quality setting. It reads as a privacy feature and buys reliability for free.
Find the metric practitioners already eyeball, instrument it, and ship the delta. A number turns a vibe into a product.
Move the sensitive step to the user's machine, then prove it with an auditable claim (no egress, local model hash, exportable data).
Take the constraint you were going to write a workaround for, and make it the headline. Broken-and-proud beats blocked-and-polished.
inspiration_intel.naive_version_vs_this: A demo that needs the user to already know what to type. — then AudioNova made the step measurable, gated, or priced instead.
inspiration_intel.reuse_surface: portable to any tool with an expensive generation step
inspiration_intel.how_they_built_it: FastAPI pipeline around Qualcomm Whisper for ASR and Vall-E-X for TTS/voice cloning; the Whisper weights are optimized and quantized through Qualcomm AI Hub so the DSP/GPU paths are used; React frontend for Windows.
inspiration_intel.hard_won_lesson: Getting Whisper onto Snapdragon X's DSP and GPU needed the AI Hub optimization pipeline; quantization and pruning had to be balanced against transcription accuracy; the UI had to stay usable while exposing voice cloning.
inspiration_intel.proof_points: Reported up to 2x faster transcription and ~35% lower power draw on Snapdragon X versus the unoptimized path; modular design so new voices, languages and audio effects can be added without a rewrite.
inspiration_intel.next_moves: Emotional intonation and prosody controls, ports to other Snapdragon devices, and partnerships with assistive-technology and healthcare users.

audionova.quote: FastAPI pipeline around Qualcomm Whisper for ASR and Vall-E-X for TTS/voice cloning; the Whisper weights are optimized and quantized through Qualcomm AI Hub so the DSP/GPU paths are used; React frontend for Windows.

audit.worth_note: 547 likes and a staff feature on a Windows-on-Snapdragon app is not luck: it deletes the cloud bill, the latency and the privacy argument at once. Held back from 'breakthrough' because on-device TTS is a crowded field and the moat here is toolchain work (AI Hub quantisation), not a new capability.

audit.what_to_steal: Make the hardware path the product, not the fallback: quantise and route to DSP/GPU deliberately, then publish the delta against your own unoptimised path (2x speed, ~35% power) as the headline number instead of a model name.
audit.what_breaks_first: Two things: cloning quality across accents and speakers, and the install base — Windows on Snapdragon X is a small denominator, so distribution breaks long before the models do. Voice cloning consent/retention is also unspecified in the page, which you must not inherit.

greenlight-nine-agent-production-crew.name: Greenlight - Nine-Agent Production Crew
greenlight-nine-agent-production-crew.summary: Nine agents turn a screenplay into a film - reading, casting, prompting, shooting, checking their own footage - and quote you the cost and the odds before spending a cent.

inspiration_intel.the_wedge: Their starting insight: Video models are good enough for anyone to make a film, but they levy an entry fee: you must already know which words work, which quality tier to pick, and what three minutes of footage will cost. Screenwriters and novelists with finished work should not have
inspiration_intel.what_it_does: Drop a screenplay. Nine agents read it whole, split it into chapters and shots, cast characters, write the prompts, generate footage, then review their own output and fold failures into the retry instruction. The user only presses keep or again. Cost and success odds are quoted per chapter before anything is generated.
steal_this: Find the metric practitioners already eyeball, instrument it, and ship the delta. A number turns a vibe into a product.
Name the roles, give each a single responsibility and an output contract, and let the handoffs be where quality is enforced.
Model your most expensive operation as a priced quote with an expected-retry figure. Users forgive slowness, not surprise bills.
Classify each step as judgement vs. format vs. volume, then route. Save the frontier model for the one call everything downstream depends on.
inspiration_intel.naive_version_vs_this: A demo that needs the user to already know what to type. — then Greenlight - Nine-Agent Production Crew made the step measurable, gated, or priced instead.
inspiration_intel.reuse_surface: portable to any agent that touches production data
inspiration_intel.how_they_built_it: One Cloud Run service shipping frontend and backend together; the Gemini family on Vertex AI assigned by shape of work (Pro for whole-screenplay reasoning and chapter splitting, Flash for well-formatted prompt writing and counting, Flash-Lite for high-volume low-judgement batches); Firestore for state, Cloud Storage fo
inspiration_intel.hard_won_lesson: A $150 credit budget against ~$1 per ten seconds of footage meant every failure cost real money, which is why success-rate prediction and a cost ladder exist at all. Gates were implemented as schema state transitions rather than prompts, because a probabilistic component cannot guarantee a hard requ
inspiration_intel.proof_points: Measured that locking a character reference before shooting lifts first-pass shot success from 29% to 49% and cuts expected retry cost from $1.86 to $1.17, for about two cents per candidate image; style buttons carry an explicit odds adjustment because photorealistic rates ~35% first-pass against ~5
inspiration_intel.next_moves: Wider style support, per-chapter reshoot workflows at higher quality tiers, and letting the accumulated verdicts drive estimates for other users' projects.

greenlight-nine-agent-production-crew.quote: One Cloud Run service shipping frontend and backend together; the Gemini family on Vertex AI assigned by shape of work (Pro for whole-screenplay reasoning and chapter splitting, Flash for well-formatted prompt writing…

audit.worth_note: The wedge is not 'AI video' — it is pricing a generation step before you commit and then making your own logged outcomes the estimator. That transfers to anything with an expensive call (image gen, agent runs, transcription at volume). Not 'breakthrough' only because it ships as one team's v1 with no public code to adopt.

build_is_real.why: no repository published, so the build cannot be read

limits_disclosed.why: the team named what the system itself cannot do (fail)

numbers_add_up.why: first-pass success 29% before casting → 49% after (recomputed: 20 points of success for $0.02 of candidates; expected retry cost falls $1.86 → $1.17); cost ladder: $0.02 candidate / $1 shot / $20 segment (recomputed: a 12-shot chapter quoted at ~$4.50 is consistent with ~$0.375/shot at the tier used, i.e. the ladder is not the naive 12×$1)

stack_consistency.why: no repo to cross-check the declared stack against

test_or_eval_evidence.why: a measured evaluation with a stated denominator is described on the page (an A/B comparison or a logged-outcome harness counts; a bare 'we tested it' does not)

assumptions: assume 1 engineer + 1 designer, 6 weeks, and real spend money for the generation ladder (their full film priced ~$238)
you can start smaller: one shot class, one priced gate, one table of verdicts — the calibration view is what takes the weeks
the character-reference locking is the part that needs image-model skill, not plumbing
clone_cost.why: the agent choreography is a weekend; the honest parts are the ledger, the calibration views, and the locked-identity image pipeline

audit.what_to_steal: Two moves, and they compose: (1) quote the cost and the pass rate before the button, and push every hesitation down the price ladder (settle a character at $0.02, not $1); (2) log every verdict row into a store you can query, then let the estimate switch from your priors to the user's own measured numbers and label which one they are reading, with sample size. Also steal 'the money gate is a schema transition, not a prompt'.
audit.what_breaks_first: The success-rate estimate. Below a few hundred logged shots per shot class the displayed percentage is a prior wearing a lab coat, so build the calibration view (predicted vs observed) in week one or you are shipping confidence theatre. Second to break: prompt-injection-free subtitle burn-in on a fresh container, which is exactly the bug they documented (ffmpeg exits 0 with no fonts).
